desc:
There are n fuel stations on a circular road. Station i gives gas[i] units of fuel when you reach it, and driving from station i to station (i + 1) % n burns cost[i] units. You drive clockwise only.

Choose a starting station, begin with an empty tank, collect its fuel and drive. The start is valid if you can return to it after a full circle without the tank ever becoming negative.

Return the number of valid starting stations (possibly 0).

gas = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], cost = [3, 4, 5, 1, 2] -> 1   (only station 3)
gas = [2, 2, 2], cost = [2, 2, 2]             -> 3
gas = [2, 3, 4], cost = [3, 4, 3]             -> 0
hints: Simulating from every start works in O(n2). Write the trip as prefix sums of d[i] = gas[i] - cost[i] to see what 'valid' means.
Start s is valid exactly when every prefix sum of d taken from s (one full lap) is non-negative. With the circle unrolled to length 2n and prefix array P, that is: min(P[s+1..s+n]) ≥ P[s].
You need the minimum of every window of n consecutive prefix values. A monotonic deque gives all of these in O(n) total.
editorial: Let d[i] = gas[i] - cost[i] and double the array so the circle becomes a line of length 2n. Define P[0] = 0 and P[j+1] = P[j] + d[j % n]. Starting at station s, the tank after the k-th leg is P[s+k] - P[s]. The start is valid when this is at least 0 for k = 1..n.

So for each s we need the minimum of the window P[s+1..s+n] and compare it with P[s]. These windows slide by one, so a monotonic deque (indices with increasing P values) gives each window minimum in amortised O(1). Count the starts that pass.

This also contains the classic single-answer problem: if the total sum is negative nothing passes, and the valid starts are exactly the stations right after the position where the unrolled prefix sum is at its minimum (and ties). Time O(n), space O(n).
